section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The Scaling Factor
section_1.content: Introduce the determinant as a 'scaling factor' of a linear transformation. Explain that when a matrix transforms space, it stretches or squishes shapes. The determinant tells us how much the area (or volume) changes.
section_1.example: Visualize a unit square with a cat inside. When the matrix is applied, the square becomes a parallelogram. The determinant is the factor by which the cat's area increased or decreased.

section_2.title: Prerequisite: The 2x2 Case
section_2.content: Recall the coordinate basis vectors [1,0] and [0,1]. Explain that a 2x2 matrix maps these to new vectors. The determinant is the signed area of the parallelogram formed by these two new vectors.
section_2.example: Show a 2x2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]]. Visualize the vectors (a, c) and (b, d) creating a shaded region; the area is |ad - bc|.

section_3.title: Negative Determinants and Orientation
section_3.content: Explain the concept of 'orientation.' If the determinant is negative, it means the transformation flipped the space (like a mirror image), effectively reversing the order of basis vectors.
section_3.example: Use a digital character's 'left hand' and 'right hand.' If the determinant is negative, the hands swap sides relative to each other.

section_4.title: The Zero Determinant: Dimensional Collapse
section_4.content: Discuss what happens when the determinant is zero. The transformation squashes the shape into a lower dimension (a line or a point), meaning the area becomes zero.
section_4.example: An animation of a 3D robot arm flattening a 3D cube into a 2D plane; the 'volume' becomes zero, representing a non-invertible matrix.

section_5.title: Summary and Connection
section_5.content: Synthesize the concepts: Det > 1 (Expansion), 0 < Det < 1 (Contraction), Det = 0 (Collapse), Det < 0 (Flip). Connect this to system solvability (if det=0, the system has no unique solution).
section_5.example: Final slide showing a 'Scaling Dial' moving from 0 to 2, with a visual shape morphing in real-time.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Negative Determinants and Orientation", [
            "Orientation defines the handedness of space.",
            "Negative determinants signify a spatial flip.",
            "Mirroring reverses the order of basis vectors."
        ])
        
        # Helper to create a handedness object
        def create_hand():
            # A stylized hand shape
            palm = Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5)
            finger = Rectangle(height=0.4, width=0.15, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).next_to(palm, UP, buff=-0.1)
            thumb = Rectangle(height=0.15, width=0.4, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).next_to(palm, RIGHT, buff=-0.1)
            return VGroup(palm, finger, thumb)

        hand = create_hand()
        self.place_at_grid(hand, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.add(hand)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        # Flip the hand (Transformation)
        self.play(ApplyMethod(hand.flip, RIGHT))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Indicate basis vectors
        vec_x = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*0.8, color=RED).next_to(hand, DOWN)
        vec_y = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=UP*0.8, color=GREEN).next_to(hand, LEFT)
        self.add(vec_x, vec_y)
        self.play(Rotate(VGroup(vec_x, vec_y), angle=PI, about_point=hand.get_center()))
        self.wait(2)
